title: incident playbook surfacing: inline checklistlets, escalation lattice, and postmortem quickbind
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem statement: On-call responders lose precious minutes searching for the correct runbook section, escalation steps, or the postmortem anchor when an alert fires. Current alert cards link to long-runbooks and external docs; they don’t surface the minimal, time-sensitive actions (checklistlets), nor do they present a compact escalation lattice tailored to team rotations and on-call tiers. Goal: design compact, inline ‘playbooklets’ that attach to alerts and incident timelines, provide checklistlets (2–6 step micro-checklists), show an escalation lattice based on rota metadata, and include a one-click ‘postmortem quickbind’ that opens a pre-populated postmortem skeleton linked to the incident. The experience should reduce mean time to acknowledgment and mean time to remediation for first-response tasks.
background: This work complements recent SLO-aware alert composer updates and the runbook extraction experiments in DES-31299. Engineering has added APIs to fetch rota metadata, on-call contacts, and a runbook snippets endpoint (ENG-4382). Product wants an experiment in a single-tenant customer org with high incident velocity before a broader rollout.
constraints: must work on mobile and desktop console flows
compact UI must not increase alert card height by >30% in list view
must respect RBAC for runbook visibility
performance: additional API calls should be cached for 2 minutes to avoid throttling
proposed_flows: Alert list view: hover/expand reveals 1–2 checklistlets and action shortcuts
Incident timeline: playbooklet pinned to top with current step highlighted and 'next' button
On-call handoff drawer: show escalation lattice, primary/secondary contacts, and a message template to notify next tier
Postmortem quickbind: prefill title, timeline anchors, and attach related alert IDs
acceptance_criteria: Checklistlets render in alert list and incident timeline with working 'mark done' state
Escalation lattice shows correct on-call contacts per rota and links to contact methods
Postmortem quickbind opens a draft with alert IDs and a link back to the incident
Prototype validated in 3 design reviews with at least two engineering feasibility notes addressed
Performance impact measured: <100ms median added latency for expanded alert render in staging org
metrics: percentage of incidents with postmortem quickbind used
design_decisions: Use a micro-checklist pattern (compact pills with trailing '...' overflow to full runbook)
Escalation lattice should be visualized as horizontal tiers (primary -> secondary -> on-call escalation) to minimize cognitive load
Postmortem quickbind will open a modal to allow edits before saving to avoid accidental creation

notes: Aim for a small, high-value experiment in one or two customer orgs. Emphasize first-response time savings and low cognitive load. If results show >10% reduction in TTA and >20% adoption of quickbind, target a phased rollout with configuration toggles for org preferences.
